examples.en: I put a protective film over my phone screen.
Why are you trying to pin the blame on me?

examples.ko: 오래된 소파에 새 천을 덧씌워서 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I put a new cover over the old sofa and keep using it.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 그림 위에 투명 필름을 덧씌웠어요.
examples.en: My friend laid a clear film over my drawing.

examples.ko: 그 사람에게 나쁜 이미지를 덧씌우지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't stick a bad image on that person.

examples.ko: 이미 끝난 일에 새 누명을 덧씌우면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't pin a new false charge on something that is already over.

explain: 물건 위에 한 겹 더 씌울 때도 쓰지만, 실제로는 '누명을 덧씌우다', '이미지를 덧씌우다'처럼 남에게 책임이나 나쁜 평가를 얹을 때 자주 들려요. 피동은 '덧씌워지다'예요.
explain_en: It can mean putting one more layer over something, but in real talk it often means pinning blame or a label on someone, as in '누명을 덧씌우다' or '이미지를 덧씌우다'. The passive form is '덧씌워지다'.

examples.en: Time has slipped by so fast that it's already autumn.

examples.ko: 꽃이 덧없이 지는 모습을 보면 마음이 쓸쓸해요.
examples.en: Watching flowers fade so quickly makes me feel lonely.
My youth has passed away so fleetingly.
I watched the snowman melt away for a long while.
I'm upset that all my effort ended in vain.
Happy moments feel fleetingly short.

explain: 주로 시간, 세월, 인생, 꽃처럼 금방 흘러가거나 사라지는 것과 함께 써요. 글이나 노래에 자주 나오고, 대화에서는 '허무하게'나 '금방'을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used with things that pass or vanish quickly, such as time, years, life or flowers. It often appears in writing and songs, while in conversation people may say '허무하게' or '금방' instead.

examples.ko: 그림이 마음에 안 들어서 덧칠을 했어요.
examples.en: I didn't like my painting, so I painted over it.
I painted over the graffiti on the wall with white paint.

examples.ko: 덧칠을 너무 많이 하면 색이 탁해져요.
examples.en: If you paint over too many times, the color gets muddy.

examples.ko: 손톱에 매니큐어를 한 번 더 덧칠해요.
examples.en: I put one more coat of nail polish on my nails.

examples.ko: 오래된 간판 위에 새 글씨를 덧칠했어요.
examples.en: I painted new letters over the old sign.

examples.ko: 덧칠한 부분이 마르면 다시 만져 보세요.
examples.en: Touch it again once the repainted part is dry.

explain: 보통 '덧칠하다'나 '덧칠을 하다'로 써요. 그림, 벽, 손톱처럼 이미 칠한 곳에 한 번 더 칠할 때 말해요. 처음부터 다시 칠하는 '다시 칠하다'와는 달리 원래 칠 위에 겹친다는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '덧칠하다' or '덧칠을 하다' for painting again on a spot that is already painted, such as a picture, wall or nails. Unlike '다시 칠하다', it strongly suggests layering over the original paint.

en: in a manner of dancing with joy

examples.ko: 할머니가 신이 나서 덩실덩실 춤을 추셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother was so excited that she danced happily.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 온 가족이 덩실덩실 어깨춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: At the news of passing, the whole family swayed their shoulders in a joyful dance.

examples.ko: 음악이 나오자 아이들이 덩실덩실 몸을 흔들어요.
examples.en: When the music starts, the children sway their bodies joyfully.

examples.ko: 기뻐서 덩실 일어나 춤을 추고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I was so happy that I wanted to jump up and dance.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 이기자 아빠가 덩실덩실 좋아하셨어요.
examples.en: When our team won, Dad celebrated with a joyful dance.

examples.ko: 축제 날에는 거리에서 사람들이 덩실덩실 춤을 춰요.
examples.en: On festival day, people dance joyfully in the streets.

explain: 대부분 '덩실덩실'로 반복해서 쓰고, 기쁘고 흥겨워서 어깨를 들썩이며 추는 춤에 어울려요. 뒤에는 '춤을 추다'가 자주 와요. 일상 대화에서는 '신나게 춤추다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used doubled as '덩실덩실' and fits a joyful dance with shoulders swaying. '춤을 추다' often follows it. In everyday talk people also say '신나게 춤추다'.

examples.en: The children dance happily to the song.
Grandfather is in a good mood and swaying his shoulders joyfully.
On festival day, people sway and dance in the streets.
She looked cute dancing around in her excitement.
As soon as the music came on, everyone started dancing joyfully.
It's nothing to dance around about like that.

explain: 기뻐서 몸이나 어깨를 흥겹게 움직일 때 써요. '덩실덩실 춤추다'와 같은 느낌이지만 이 동사는 춤 자체보다 들썩이는 움직임을 말할 때 자연스러워요. 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It describes moving your body or shoulders happily out of joy. It feels like '덩실덩실 춤추다', but this verb sounds more natural for the bouncing movement itself. It appears more in writing and stories.

examples.en: The ball rolled down the stairs.
A pencil rolled off the desk.
The apples come out of the bag and roll away.

examples.ko: 동전이 데구루루 굴러서 침대 밑으로 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The coin rolled under the bed.

examples.ko: 귤이 데구루루 굴러서 문 앞까지 갔어요.
examples.en: The tangerine rolled all the way to the door.

examples.ko: 아기가 던진 공이 데구루루 굴러 왔어요.
examples.en: The ball the baby threw came rolling over.

explain: 작고 단단하거나 둥근 물건이 굴러가는 모양과 소리에 써요. 뒤에는 '구르다', '굴러가다', '떨어지다'가 자주 와요. '데굴데굴'은 계속 구르는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It describes a small, hard or round object rolling along, with its sound. Verbs like '구르다', '굴러가다' and '떨어지다' often follow. '데굴데굴' feels more like continuous rolling.

examples.en: I'm still a bit distant with my cousin since we met after a long time.

examples.ko: 동료와 싸운 뒤로 서로 데면데면하게 지내요.
examples.en: Since the fight with my coworker, we've been cool toward each other.
I'm shy with strangers, so I tend to be distant at first.
Why are you so cold to me these days?
We used to be distant, but we got closer after the trip.
We're siblings, but we're so distant with each other that it feels awkward.

explain: '서먹서먹하다'와 가깝지만, 데면데면하다는 태도가 살갑지 않고 무덤덤한 쪽에 가까워요. 친해질 만한 사이인데 정이 없어 보일 때 많이 써요. 반대로 따뜻하고 가까운 느낌은 '살갑다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is close to '서먹서먹하다', but 데면데면하다 leans toward a cold, unaffectionate attitude. It is often used when two people could be close but seem to have no warmth. The opposite, warm and friendly, is '살갑다'.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 도굴된 유물이 돌아왔다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the news that relics stolen from graves were returned to the museum.

examples.ko: 옛 무덤은 도굴 때문에 많이 훼손됐어요.
examples.en: Many old tombs were badly damaged because of grave robbing.
They installed CCTV at the historic site to prevent looting.
In the movie, the main character visits a looting site.
Cultural assets lost to looting are hard to recover.

examples.ko: 그 지역은 도굴이 자주 일어나서 경비가 강해요.
examples.en: Looting often happens in that area, so security is tight.

explain: 무덤이나 유적을 몰래 파서 물건을 가져가는 일이라 주로 뉴스, 역사, 문화재 이야기에서 나와요. '도굴하다', '도굴되다'로도 쓰고, 일상에서는 '무덤을 파헤치다'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in news, history and talk about cultural assets. It is also used as '도굴하다' and '도굴되다', and in daily talk people may spell it out as '무덤을 파헤치다'.

examples.ko: 그는 낡은 도그마에서 벗어나 새로 생각했어요.
examples.en: He broke free from old dogma and thought anew.

examples.ko: 그 이론은 과학이 아니라 도그마에 가까워요.
examples.en: That theory is closer to dogma than to science.

examples.ko: 도그마에 빠지면 다른 의견을 듣기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once you fall into dogma, it's hard to listen to other opinions.

examples.ko: 종교적인 도그마가 사회 갈등을 키웠다고 해요.
examples.en: They say religious dogma made social conflict worse.
We need a habit of questioning dogma.

examples.ko: 교수님은 하나의 도그마만 믿지 말라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The professor told us not to believe in just one dogma.

explain: 비판 없이 굳게 믿는 신조나 주장을 조금 나쁘게 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻의 한국어로 '독단'이나 '교조'도 쓰는데, 도그마는 논설이나 수업에서 자주 보여요. 좋은 뜻의 '신념'과는 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to a belief or claim held firmly without questioning, with a somewhat negative tone. Korean words like '독단' and '교조' are close, but 도그마 often appears in essays and lectures. It feels different from the positive '신념' (conviction).

examples.en: Our company handed the construction work over on contract.

examples.ko: 도급 계약서를 쓰기 전에 조건을 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked the terms before writing the contract agreement.

examples.ko: 도급을 받은 업체가 다음 달에 일을 시작해요.
examples.en: The company that won the contract starts work next month.

examples.ko: 이 일은 월급이 아니라 도급으로 일해요.
examples.en: I do this job on a contract basis, not a monthly salary.

examples.ko: 도급 금액이 너무 낮아서 계약하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The contract amount was too low, so I didn't sign.

examples.ko: 건설 현장에서는 도급 관계가 복잡한 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: At construction sites, contracting relationships are often complicated.

explain: 일이 끝나는 것을 약속하고 맡거나 맡기는 계약을 말해요. 월급을 받으며 일하는 고용과 달라서 뉴스나 건설, 회사 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 도급받은 일을 다시 다른 곳에 맡기면 '하도급'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is a contract where someone promises to complete a job, taking it on or handing it out. It differs from being employed for a salary, and often appears in news and talk about construction or companies. Passing a contracted job on to another firm is called '하도급'.

examples.ko: 옛이야기 속 도깨비방망이는 두드리면 뭐든 나와요.
examples.en: In old tales, anything comes out when you knock the goblin's club.

examples.ko: 도깨비방망이가 있다면 먼저 집을 만들고 싶어요.
examples.en: If I had a goblin's magic club, I'd make a house first.
The child plays swinging a stick like a goblin's club.
There is no magic-wand solution in this world.
In the storybook, gold poured out when the goblin's club was struck.

examples.ko: 도깨비방망이를 갖고 싶다고 말하는 아이가 많아요.
examples.en: Many children say they want a goblin's magic club.

explain: 전래동화에서 도깨비가 가진 방망이로, 두드리면 원하는 것이 나와요. 지금은 '도깨비방망이 같은 해결책'처럼 한 번에 다 해결해 줄 것 같은 만능 방법을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 도깨비방망이 같은 해결책을 찾지 말고 하나씩 해 봐요.
phrases.en: Don't look for a magic-wand solution; let's try one thing at a time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단번에 문제를 해결해 줄 것 같은 만능 방법을 말해요. 보통 그런 방법은 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means an all-purpose fix that seems to solve a problem at once. It is usually used to say that no such fix exists.

explain_en: This is the club that goblins hold in folktales, and whatever you wish for comes out when you strike it. Today it is also used in phrases like '도깨비방망이 같은 해결책' for an all-purpose fix that seems to solve everything at once.

examples.en: They say people in the old days feared the goblin fires on night roads.

examples.ko: 어두운 산길에서 도깨비불 같은 빛이 보였어요.
examples.en: I saw a light like a will-o'-the-wisp on the dark mountain path.
Grandmother told me a story about goblin fires.

examples.ko: 묘지 근처에 도깨비불이 나타난다는 소문이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a rumor that a goblin fire appears near the graveyard.

examples.ko: 밤하늘에 반짝이는 도깨비불 때문에 아이가 울었어요.
examples.en: The child cried because of the goblin fire flickering in the night.

examples.ko: 도깨비불을 봤다는 사람이 마을에 몇 명 있어요.
examples.en: A few people in the village say they have seen a goblin fire.

explain: 밤에 들이나 산에서 보인다는 정체를 알 수 없는 불로, 도깨비가 만든다고 믿던 데서 온 이름이에요. 주로 옛이야기, 전설, 괴담에서 나와요. 지금 일상 대화에서는 거의 이야기 속 소재로만 들려요.
explain_en: This is a mysterious fire said to be seen in fields or mountains at night, and the name comes from the belief that goblins made it. It mostly appears in old tales, legends and ghost stories. In today's conversation it is mostly just a story topic.

examples.ko: 동생이 거짓말을 하자 엄마가 도끼눈으로 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: When my sister lied, Mom glared at her.
Please don't glare at me like that.

examples.ko: 친구가 도끼눈을 하고 저를 노려봐서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: My friend glared at me with sharp eyes, and it was scary.
They asked in an accusing glare, so it was hard to answer.
My boss checked the documents with a sharp, stern look.

examples.ko: 아이들이 도끼눈을 한 채 서로 눈치를 봤어요.
examples.en: The kids eyed each other with glaring looks.

explain: 화가 나거나 미워서 눈을 모나게 뜨고 볼 때 쓰는 말이에요. '도끼눈을 뜨다', '도끼눈으로 보다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '째려보다'가 있는데, 도끼눈은 표정과 눈매를 그릴 때 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: This describes eyes opened sharply in anger or dislike, used as '도끼눈을 뜨다' or '도끼눈으로 보다'. '째려보다' is similar, but 도끼눈 sounds more natural when describing the look on someone's face.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아기 등을 도닥도닥 두드려 줬어요.
examples.en: Mom gently patted the baby's back.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 어깨를 도닥도닥 두드려 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend gave my shoulder a few gentle pats.
Grandmother gently patted the blanket for me.

examples.ko: 도닥도닥 소리를 내며 빵 반죽을 두드렸어요.
examples.en: I patted the dough, making a soft tapping sound.
I gently patted the child's bottom to put him to sleep.

examples.ko: 강아지 머리를 도닥도닥 가볍게 두드려 줬어요.
examples.en: I gave the puppy's head a few light pats.

explain: 가볍게 여러 번 두드리는 모양이에요. 아기를 달래거나 위로할 때 어울려요. '토닥토닥'도 비슷한 느낌으로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes tapping lightly several times, which suits soothing a baby or comforting someone. '토닥토닥' is a similar word with a similar feel.

examples.ko: 엄마가 우는 아기의 등을 도닥여 줬어요.
examples.en: Mom patted the crying baby's back gently.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 어깨를 도닥이며 괜찮다고 했어요.
examples.en: My friend patted my shoulder and said it's okay.
I pat the child's chest until he falls asleep.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손자의 등을 도닥이며 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sang while patting her grandson's back.
I patted down the soil to cover the seeds.
On hard days, I comfort myself and fall asleep.

explain: 가볍게 톡톡 두드려서 달래거나 다질 때 써요. 등, 어깨, 가슴처럼 사람의 몸이나 흙을 목적어로 많이 써요. '토닥이다'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means to pat lightly to soothe or to firm something down. It is often used with a person's back, shoulder or chest, or with soil. '토닥이다' is a similar word.

en: point of arrival; finish line; destination

examples.en: I can see the end point of the marathon over there.

examples.ko: 이 길의 도달점은 작은 바닷가 마을이에요.
examples.en: The end of this road is a small seaside town.
The goal of studying isn't only exam scores.

examples.ko: 우리가 생각한 도달점과 결과가 많이 달랐어요.
examples.en: The result was very different from the goal we had in mind.
The closer I got to the end point, the more energy I felt.

examples.ko: 이번 프로젝트의 최종 도달점을 같이 정해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's decide together on the final goal of this project.

explain: 실제 길의 끝뿐 아니라 공부나 일에서 목표로 하는 마지막 지점에도 써요. 장소를 말할 때는 '목적지', 달리기에서는 '결승선'처럼 더 구체적인 말을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the end of a real route and also to the final point you aim for in studying or work. For places people may use more concrete words like '목적지', and for races '결승선'.

examples.ko: 이 악보에는 도돌이표가 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: This sheet music has two repeat signs.

examples.ko: 도돌이표를 만나면 앞으로 돌아가서 다시 연주해요.
examples.en: When you meet a repeat sign, you go back and play again.

examples.ko: 선생님이 도돌이표 부분을 한 번 더 치라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told me to play the repeated section once more.

examples.ko: 도돌이표를 못 봐서 중간에 끝내 버렸어요.
examples.en: I didn't see the repeat sign and ended in the middle.
Every meeting is like a loop, and it's frustrating.
My days repeat the same, like a loop.

explain: 악보에서 앞부분으로 돌아가 다시 연주하라고 알려 주는 기호예요. 요즘은 같은 일이나 말이 끝없이 되풀이될 때 '도돌이표 같다'고도 해요.

phrases.en: Our conversations always go around in circles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 이야기나 상황이 끝없이 되풀이되어 답답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the same topic or situation repeats endlessly and feels frustrating.

explain_en: This is the sign in sheet music telling you to go back and play a section again. Today people also say '도돌이표 같다' when the same things or words repeat endlessly.

examples.en: The market the day before a holiday is as chaotic as a bazaar.
On the first day of the sale, the store turned into a zoo.

examples.ko: 사람이 너무 많아서 역 앞이 도떼기시장 같았어요.
examples.en: There were so many people that the area in front of the station was a madhouse.
During breaks, the classroom turns into a madhouse.

examples.ko: 도떼기시장에서 물건을 사려면 큰 소리로 말해야 해요.
examples.en: To buy things in a chaotic market, you have to speak loudly.
Yesterday's event hall was a madhouse, so I was overwhelmed.

explain: 사람이 많고 시끄러워서 정신없는 장소나 상황을 시장에 빗대어 말해요. 시장 자체보다 행사장, 교실, 매장 같은 곳에 비유로 쓸 때가 많아요. 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It compares a crowded, noisy, chaotic place or situation to a market. It is often used figuratively for event halls, classrooms or stores rather than markets themselves. It carries a slightly negative tone.

en: whisper to each other; murmur affectionately

examples.en: The children are murmuring to each other under the blanket.
I can hear my parents talking softly in the living room.

examples.ko: 친구와 밤새 도란거리다 보니 아침이 됐어요.
examples.en: I chatted quietly with my friend all night, and morning came.
Someone was murmuring in the room, so I woke up.
The family gathers and eats dinner chatting warmly.

examples.ko: 연인이 벤치에서 도란거리는 모습이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: The couple murmuring on the bench looks warm.

explain: 가까운 사람끼리 낮고 정답게 이야기하는 소리에 써요. 시끄럽게 떠드는 것과는 반대 느낌이에요. 부사 '도란도란'과 함께 '도란도란 이야기하다'로 쓰는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: It describes close people talking in low, friendly voices, the opposite of noisy chatter. The adverb '도란도란' is also often used, as in '도란도란 이야기하다'.

examples.ko: 이 호수는 겨울 철새 도래지로 유명해요.
examples.en: This lake is famous as a winter stop for migratory birds.
I went to a migratory bird site and saw cranes.
Please walk quietly near the bird sanctuary.

examples.ko: 개발 때문에 철새 도래지가 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: Migratory bird sites are shrinking because of development.
They restricted entry to protect the bird site.

examples.ko: 올겨울에는 도래지에 새가 많이 오지 않았어요.
examples.en: This winter, not many birds came to the site.

explain: 실제로는 주로 '철새 도래지'로 써요. 철새가 계절에 따라 날아와 머무는 곳을 말해요. 뉴스, 여행, 환경 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 새가 먹이를 찾아 쉬어 가는 호수나 갯벌을 가리킬 때가 많아요.
explain_en: In practice it is mostly used as '철새 도래지', a place where migratory birds arrive and stay by season. It often appears in news, travel and environmental topics, usually for lakes or tidal flats where birds rest and feed.

examples.en: I cut out the rotten part of the apple with a knife.
Cut out the potato sprouts before cooking.
I cut out just the photo from the paper and pasted it.
The doctor said he cut out the bad part.
It was a pain like having my heart cut out.
I cut a coupon out of the magazine and took it along.

explain: 칼이나 가위로 일부를 둥글게 파내듯 잘라낼 때 써요. 그냥 '자르다'보다 안쪽 한 부분만 떼어 낸다는 느낌이 강해요. 아픔을 말할 때 '가슴을 도려내다'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 그 소식은 가슴을 도려내는 것처럼 아팠어요.
phrases.en: That news hurt as if my heart were being cut out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 자르는 것이 아니라 아주 큰 슬픔이나 아픔을 강하게 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean actual cutting; it strongly expresses deep sorrow or pain.

explain_en: It is used for cutting out a part with a knife or scissors, as if scooping it out. Compared with plain '자르다', it strongly suggests removing just one inner part. It is also used figuratively for pain, as in '가슴을 도려내다'.

examples.en: I found salamander eggs by the stream.
They say salamanders are often seen in clear valleys.
The child caught a salamander and showed it to me.
The salamander slowly crept into a crack in the rock.
I went to the valley to take photos of salamanders.
Salamanders live in the pond in the forest.

explain: 도마뱀과 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 도롱뇽은 물가에 사는 양서류이고 도마뱀은 파충류예요. 표준어는 '도롱뇽'이고, 맑은 계곡이나 연못 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: People often confuse it with a lizard (도마뱀), but a 도롱뇽 is an amphibian living near water, while a 도마뱀 is a reptile. The standard spelling is '도롱뇽', and it often comes up in talk about clear valleys and ponds.

examples.ko: 벽에 도료를 바르기 전에 먼저 닦아요.
examples.en: I wipe the wall first before applying paint.

examples.ko: 이 도료는 물에 강해서 욕실에 좋아요.
examples.en: This coating resists water, so it's good for bathrooms.
The paint smell was strong, so I opened the window.

examples.ko: 배에 칠하는 도료는 일반 페인트와 달라요.
examples.en: The coating applied to ships differs from regular paint.
I applied a new coat of paint to the old iron gate.
They say it takes a day for the paint to dry.

explain: 페인트, 니스, 래커처럼 표면에 칠하는 재료를 두루 가리켜요. 일상 대화에서는 '페인트'를 많이 쓰고, '도료'는 공사 설명이나 제품 설명, 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It broadly covers materials applied to a surface, like paint, varnish and lacquer. In daily talk '페인트' is commonly used, while '도료' often appears in construction explanations, product descriptions and news.
